findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:591 — Handler returns a hardcoded, non-localized `{ message: "Guests added" }` payload that the client never reads (client shows its own translated toast on success), so the response shape carries dead/inconsistent data that any future or external caller relying on `message` for the actual outcome text would get untranslated English regardless of locale.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:440 — addGuestsHandler is a 150+ line function mixing auth, prisma queries, CalendarEvent construction, calendar sync, and email sending — should be decomposed for testability and future changes.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:464 — isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `&&` (requires both admin AND owner) but the name implies OR, making the permission check misleading to future readers/maintainers.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx:401 — The comment "Unreachable code but required for type safety" plus the dead-end throw is boilerplate copy-pasted from other handlers' cache pattern, adding noise without real behavior.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:588 — Error from sendAddGuestsEmails is caught and only console.log'd ("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") with no structured logger, error object, or context — makes failures unactionable and inconsistent with app logging conventions.

packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts:296 — AttendeeAddGuestsEmail and organizer-add-guests-email.ts:338 OrganizerAddGuestsEmail duplicate near-identical getNodeMailerPayload bodies (icalEvent construction, subject formatting, getTextBody call) differing only in recipient/role — logic should be shared via a helper to avoid drift when one is updated but not the other.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:232 — sendAddGuestsEmails silently branches per-attendee between AttendeeScheduledEmail and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail based on newGuests.includes(attendee.email), coupling this function to knowledge of two unrelated email template families instead of a single dedicated template with a parameter.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:629 — The component duplicates near-identical "add email" Button markup/handler in both the empty-list branch (line 688) and non-empty-list branch (line 668), which could be unified into one control to reduce duplication.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:501 — guestsFullDetails hardcodes name: "" for all new guests with no way to supply a name, silently discarding any future name input and requiring a coupled change here if the UI ever adds a name field.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:583 — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) is called without a try/catch after the DB write at line 510 already persisted the new attendees, so a calendar-sync failure leaves the booking's guest list inconsistent with the actual calendar event and throws an unhandled error back through the mutation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:60 — Guest emails are compared to `blacklistedGuestEmails` (lowercased) without lowercasing `guest` first, so the blacklist filter is trivially bypassed with a different email case (e.g. `Blocked@x.com` vs `blocked@x.com`)

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:591 — Handler returns a hardcoded, non-localized `{ message: "Guests added" }` payload that the client never reads (client shows its own translated toast on success), so the response shape carries dead/inconsistent data that any future or external caller relying on `message` for the actual outcome text would get untranslated English regardless of locale.

adjudication.rationale: The handler does return a hardcoded `{ message: "Guests added" }` at the end of `addGuestsHandler`, and the new client code (`AddGuestsDialog`) does not read the mutation result (it shows its own `t("guests_added")` toast in `onSuccess`). However, this does not introduce a verifiable bug/correctness issue in the diff: the response shape being unused/redundant is not inherently defective, and the claim about “future or external callers” relying on `message` is speculative. Also, server API responses are often intentionally non-localized, so “untranslated English” is not clearly a defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a relatively long `addGuestsHandler` (~170 lines) that mixes authorization, Prisma access, CalendarEvent construction, calendar sync, and email sending, but this is a maintainability/refactoring suggestion rather than a concrete bug/security/correctness defect. Additionally, the cited location `addGuests.handler.ts:440` is not verifiable in the new file shown (it is ~174 lines), indicating the finding is not grounded in the diff as written.

matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

This matches the golden issue that the permission logic should use `||` so either role grants access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx:401 — The comment "Unreachable code but required for type safety" plus the dead-end throw is boilerplate copy-pasted from other handlers' cache pattern, adding noise without real behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include the exact comment and fallback `if (!UNSTABLE_HANDLER_CACHE.addGuests) { throw new Error("Failed to load handler"); }` after a preceding assignment, making it effectively redundant in normal execution. However, this is not a bug/security/correctness defect; it’s a stylistic/boilerplate pattern used elsewhere for type narrowing and defensive checks. The finding is therefore a style nit rather than a verifiable problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:588 — Error from sendAddGuestsEmails is caught and only console.log'd ("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") with no structured logger, error object, or context — makes failures unactionable and inconsistent with app logging conventions.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuests.handler.ts`, the call to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that swallows the exception and only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err` or any contextual data (e.g., bookingId). This is verifiably present in the diff and would make diagnosing email-send failures difficult. (The finding’s cited line number is off, but the behavior exists.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:501 — guestsFullDetails hardcodes name: "" for all new guests with no way to supply a name, silently discarding any future name input and requiring a coupled change here if the UI ever adds a name field.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s TRPC schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema`) only accepts `guests: string[]` (emails), and the new UI component (`MultiEmail` / `AddGuestsDialog`) only collects emails—there is no name field anywhere in this change. Therefore `guestsFullDetails` setting `name: ""` is consistent with the current API/UI and is not “silently discarding” provided name input. The finding is primarily speculative about a hypothetical future UI change, and even cites a non-existent line number (the new handler is ~174 lines).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:583 — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) is called without a try/catch after the DB write at line 510 already persisted the new attendees, so a calendar-sync failure leaves the booking's guest list inconsistent with the actual calendar event and throws an unhandled error back through the mutation.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking attendees are persisted first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` (around line ~510 in the diff). After that, `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is executed without any surrounding try/catch or compensating rollback. If that calendar-sync call throws, the mutation will reject/propagate the error while the DB changes have already been committed, leaving the booking’s attendee list updated in Cal.com but potentially not reflected in the external calendar event. This is directly verifiable from the diff and is a correctness/consistency risk introduced by the ordering and lack of error handling/transactionality.
